correctness.rationale: For the explicit tangent vectors h,k the zero-sum, orthogonality and unit-length conditions are checked exactly. The standard Fourier-integral section formula is used only through ratios. In the collective path the two-coordinate factor admits an L1-uniform order-squared expansion, and the six vanishing coordinates contribute a positive nonanalytic |s|^3 term. Beta integrals cancel the s^2 coefficient and yield J=3003*pi/512, hence the exact normalized cubic coefficient 1001*sqrt(3)/3072. A separate tangent has a negative normalized s^2 coefficient -3/2. An embedded exact SymPy verifier was executed and returned SADDLE_EXACT_OK; high-precision quadrature checks signs but is not used as the proof. These opposite perturbation signs imply a saddle for all sufficiently small nonzero real s, without claiming global optimality.

value.rationale: The n=8 sparse normal is the exact dimension where the published local stability Hessian changes from negative to positive in its collective eigenvalue, leaving an unresolved degenerate border. Determining the positive nonanalytic |s|^3 term and providing a negative transverse perturbation settles whether the conspicuous candidate is locally maximal, a genuine problem-guided structural issue rather than a chosen arbitrary parameter. The result gives an exact, checkable high-order geometric bifurcation and a meaningful obstruction to a conjectural maximizer location, without requiring resolution of the global optimization.
